For any $\lambda,\mu\in X_{*}(T)^{+}$, we have

$\Hom_{D^{\mathrm{b}}_{\mathscr{S}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})}({\mathbf{IC}}_{\lambda},{\mathbf{IC}}_{\mu}[1])=0.$

The main ingredients in the proof of Proposition 4.4 are the following facts:

•

the cohomology sheaves $\mathscr{H}^{k}({\mathbf{IC}}_{\lambda})$ vanish unless $k$ and $\dim(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda})$ have the same parity (see Lemma 4.5 below);

•

if $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\mu}\subset\overline{\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda}}$, then $\mathrm{codim}_{\overline{\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}^{\lambda}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}^{\mu})$ is even (see §3.1).

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
